name: Stripe Checkout
author: Anvil contributors
description: Finds Stripe secret keys and webhook secrets in your code, checks that the checkout success and cancel pages load, and walks you through a test-card payment, a declined card and a closed tab.

checks.title: Live Stripe secret key in the code
checks.why: A live secret (sk_live_) or restricted (rk_live_) key lets whoever has it create charges, issue refunds and read customer data on your Stripe account. If it is in front-end code, everyone who opens DevTools has it.
checks.fix: Roll the key in the Stripe dashboard now (Developers > API keys) and treat the old one as leaked. Call Stripe only from a server route that reads the key from an environment variable; the browser needs only the publishable key (pk_live_).

checks.title: Test-mode Stripe secret key in the code
checks.why: Test keys cannot move real money, but a leaked one lets anyone read and change your test data and webhooks, and it usually means the live key will end up in the same place.
checks.fix: Move the key into a server-side environment variable now, before you switch to live mode, and roll it in the Stripe dashboard.

checks.title: Stripe webhook signing secret in the code
checks.why: With the webhook signing secret, anyone can forge 'payment succeeded' events that your server will trust, and mark orders paid without paying.
checks.fix: Roll the signing secret for this endpoint (Developers > Webhooks) and read it from a server-side environment variable.

checks.title: Checkout success page at /success does not load
checks.why: After paying, Stripe sends the customer to your success URL. If that page is missing or errors, people who just paid see a broken page and often pay twice or ask for a refund. If your app uses a different success URL, ignore this and answer the test-card human check instead.
checks.fix: Make sure the success_url you pass to Stripe Checkout points at a page that exists and loads without signing in again.

checks.title: Checkout cancel page at /cancel does not load
checks.why: When a customer backs out of checkout, Stripe sends them to your cancel URL. A missing page here loses the sale. If your app uses a different cancel URL, ignore this.
checks.fix: Point cancel_url at a page that exists, ideally the cart or pricing page, so the customer can try again.

humanChecks.prompt: In test mode, does a payment with the 4242 test card go through and unlock what was bought?
steps: Make sure the app is using Stripe test keys
Start checkout and pay with card 4242 4242 4242 4242, any future expiry date and any CVC
Check that you land on the success page
Check that the purchase (plan, credits, order) is now active in the app
Check that the payment shows in the Stripe dashboard (test mode)

humanChecks.prompt: Does a declined card fail cleanly without unlocking anything?
steps: Start checkout and pay with card 4000 0000 0000 0002 (always declined)
Check that Stripe shows a decline message
Go back to the app and confirm nothing was unlocked

humanChecks.prompt: If you close the tab right after paying, does the order still become paid?
steps: Start checkout with the 4242 test card
Close the tab as soon as you click Pay, before the success page loads
Sign back in to the app a minute later
Answer Broken if the purchase is not active (the app is trusting the success page instead of a webhook)

humanChecks.prompt: Does opening the success page directly, without paying, unlock anything?
steps: Sign in as a user who has not paid
Type the success page URL into the address bar (copy any session_id from an earlier test if the URL has one)
Answer Broken if the app now treats this user as paid
